data.title: PM Anutin wants water retention areas around Bangkok
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning to study ways to develop water retention areas around Bangkok in order to prevent future floods.

data.title: Man held for ‘renting’ ID cards to underage clubgoers
data.description: KHON KAEN - Police have arrested a 19-year-old man accused of renting out national ID cards to underage youths seeking entry to entertainment venues in Khon Kaen, charging 100 baht per card.

data.title: Natthaphong says government’s flood response has failed
data.description: People’s Party leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut has called on the government to do more to help local administrative bodies recover from the floods, saying the performance so far has not been good.

data.title: Second incinerator key to solving Phuket’s waste problem
data.description: PHUKET - Authorities in this southern island province are seeking a land plot to build a second incinerator to handle a growing amount of garbage.

data.title: Anutin slams Prachin Buri district chief for mishandling flood
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has admonished Prachin Buri's Ban Sang district chief who was abruptly transferred on Wednesday after being accused of resisting cooperation and not making a sufficient effort to help flood victims in the province.

data.title: Western provinces warned of flooding, poor drainage in east
data.description: The government on Wednesday warned of possible flooding in western provinces with forecasts of heavy rain, while explaining high tides are impeding drainage of flood waters from eastern provinces Chachoengsao and Prachin Buri.

data.title: Filipino family crash into temple wall kills 3-year-old son
data.description: SURAT THANI — A three-year-old Filipino boy was killed and three other members of his family were injured after their Mitsubishi Pajero crashed into a temple wall in Ban Ta Khun district early Wednesday morning.

data.title: Armed robbers take nearly B30m from Chinese residents of Chon Buri mansion
data.description: CHON BURI: Three armed robbers held the Chinese occupants of a luxury residence at gunpoint before escaping with cash and assets worth a combined nearly 30 million baht on Tuesday.

data.title: Heavy rain in Greater Bangkok from Saturday to Monday
data.description: The Meteorological Department expects heavy rain in Greater Bangkok from Saturday to Monday as the country is reaching the end of the wet season.

data.title: 2,000 swine drown at flooded farm
data.description: Authorities expect to clear about 2,000 pig carcasses from a flooded farm in Prachin Buri by Thursday, Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Suriya Juangroongruangkit said.

data.title: Higher VAT urged amid net deficit
data.description: The government has reported a net deficit of 760 billion baht for fiscal 2025, as senators called for a higher value-added tax (VAT) and a broader tax base.

data.title: BMA steps up efforts to drain flooded communities
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) is accelerating floodwater drainage operations at Rom Klao Community Housing in Lat Krabang district.

data.title: BJT gives its MP benefit of the doubt
data.description: Digital Economy and Society Minister Chaichanok Chidchob has defended Bhumjaithai Party MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap, saying he has seen no evidence linking her husband to scam networks.

data.title: Tribute paid to Oct 6 Thammasat tragedy
data.description: Thailand's democracy "has never been fully fledged", said opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut at an event marking the 50th anniversary of the Oct 6, 1976 massacre.

data.title: Opposition set to file censure bid
data.description: People's Party leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut said on Tuesday the opposition would soon submit a no-confidence motion, with the debate expected by late October or early next month.

data.title: NHRC raises concerns over public broadcaster funding
data.description: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has expressed concern that proposed legislation to alter the funding sources of four public organisations could undermine media independence and affect fundamental public rights and freedoms.

data.title: Hospitals told to stock seven days of medicines
data.description: The Ministry of Public Health has ordered hospitals to stockpile enough medicines for at least seven days and food for 10 days ahead of more rain in the South next week.

data.title: Mother, daughters found dead after loan scam
data.description: A single mother and her two young daughters were found dead in their rented home in Pathum Thani on Tuesday after she was allegedly duped in a fraudulent loan application.

data.title: Families allege scam over taekwondo training fees
data.description: CHAIYAPHUM: Four families have asked police and the Sports Authority of Thailand (SAT) to investigate a taekwondo coach in Muang district after claiming they were ripped off.

data.title: Deluge pushes up vegetable, egg prices
data.description: Widespread flooding has disrupted agricultural production in several parts of Thailand, reducing supplies and pushing up vegetable and egg prices, Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun said.

data.title: Care home claims spark probe
data.description: The Public Health Ministry has launched an investigation into an elderly care home in Kanchanaburi's Tha Muang district following reports that residents were subjected to physical and psychological abuse and inhumane living conditions.

data.title: Eastern flooding persists
data.description: Flooding in eastern Thailand entered its seventh consecutive day, with stagnant water causing foul odours in some areas.

data.title: No signs of plague in Thailand
data.description: Thailand is closely monitoring a suspected plague case in Russia but has found no indication that the disease has entered the country, Public Health Minister Pattana Promphat said.

data.title: Substation storm fire causes Nong Chok blackout
data.description: A high-voltage substation of the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand caught fire in Nong Chok district of Bangkok during heavy rain on Tuesday.

data.title: Disease control chief allays plague concern in Russia
data.description: The Department of Disease Control (DDC) says there is no evidence of a plague outbreak in Russia and considers the risk of transmission to Thailand to be low.

data.title: Central Plains floods easing, risk moving South
data.description: Floods contiue to dominate parts of Bangkok and 27 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but the risk is moving southwards with the approach of the annual northeast monsoon.

data.title: Conned workers still waiting for refunds after hoax recruiter jailed
data.description: BURI RAM - Representatives of about 200 workers tricked into paying a recruiter for non-existent jobs in Australia on Tuesday complained to police they were still waiting to be repaid more than a year after the woman was sent to prison and ordered to refund their money.

data.title: Old woman alleges she was forcibly confined for 2 years
data.description: An elderly woman has accused her son and daughter-in-law of tricking her into entering a care centre more than two years again and kept her there against her will so they could take control of a business worth billions of baht.
